en: The *Manasvāra-śikṣā*:
I shall proclaim the *Manasvāra*, which was fashioned by Brahmā in ancient times and spoken by the venerable Yājñavalkya for the benefit of the world. 1.

Now, in the middle of a three-footed [verse], there are two unaccented syllables at the pause. Now, in the middle of a long [verse], there are unaccented syllables. "Who thee, the king of desires... (ka-stvā rājantam-advarāṇām); "Like a father, grant us... (sanaḥ pitā-iva mā naḥ); "Around thee... (pari te prāg-apāk); "O Maruts, him whose... (pra no maruto yasya yoge-yoge tavastaram); "To him he gave... (tasmā arand dhanvanaḥ parasyāḥ); "Again with strength... (punar ūrjā ni sam itam agne); "That which is thy bright... (yat te śukram); "For thee these... (tubhya imā mayi gṛhṇāmi madhu); "Honeyed winds, honeyed for us... (madhumān no agne); "Yoke thyself, O youngest one... (yukṣva tvam yaviṣṭha); "O Agni, purifier... (agne pāvaka sa naḥ pāvaka).

For the slaying of Vṛtra, for strength, let Pavamāna flow forth; O thou of wondrous luster, impelled by prayer, bring hither even those who are hidden. O Agni, you have indeed brought Mitra and Varuṇa to us; may he sacrifice to the wives. O Vāyu, O God, with all your tawny steeds whose banner is smoke, come to the Soma-draught. O Purifier, whatever today Varuṇa has protected, and whatever fault is mine, may Indra [remove it]; may the divine waters strengthen me. May the Maruts [protect] me—svāhā! (Fifty-four hundred and five.)

Now follows the three-footed [verse], with two anudātta accents: "Pradhāsinaḥ havāmahe vvyarṭha0 somāntaryaccha mahī dyauḥ saha rayyā'gniḥ priyeṣu samudrasya tvā dvayaṃ śukrajyotiścedṛṅca vaiśvānaro naḥ pāvakā naḥ sunāvamāruheyandevasya cetato rātirṭha0 satpatiṃ devasya saviturupahvare girīṇāmuccā te draviṇo dāḥ pipīṣati vvibhaktārarṭha0 havāmaha' ubhā piṣatarṭha0 hṛde tvā dvāirṭha0śatiḥ 2" [The verses are: 1. *pradhāsino havāmahe* (We invoke those who bestow abundance), *vvyarṭha0 somāntaryaccha* (O Soma, restrain within us), *mahī dyauḥ saha rayyā* (May the great heaven be with wealth), *agniḥ priyeṣu* (Agni among our dear things). 2. *samudrasya tvā* (I take you from the ocean), *dvayaṃ śukrajyotiścedṛṅca* (The pair, the bright light, and the vision), *vaiśvānaro naḥ pāvakā* (Vaiśvānara, the purifier for us), *naḥ sunāvamāruheyat* (May he cause us to ascend the good ship). 3. *devasya cetato rātirṭha0* (The gift of the conscious god), *satpatiṃ devasya saviturupahvare* (The lord of beings, in the presence of the god Savitṛ), *girīṇāmuccā te* (High above the mountains, yours), *draviṇo dāḥ* (O giver of wealth), *pipīṣati* (He desires to drink). 4. *vvibhaktārarṭha0 havāmaha* (We invoke the distributor), *ubhā piṣatarṭha0* (Both, O crusher), *hṛde tvā* (For the heart, you), *dvāirṭha0śatiḥ* (The twenty-two). 2. [End of section]

Now, those [verses] beginning and ending with three feet have their middle syllables unaccented (*anudātta*). *agne vratapate*, *susamiddhāya*, *trayaṃ*, *mano nu punar naḥ*, *ud u tyaṃ*, *tam ut tvā pāthaḥ*, *vṛṣā*, *āpo hi ṣṭhā*, *ayam agne abhyāvartin*, *agne vājasya*, *yenā samatsu*, *agne tam adya*, *namas te rudra*, *saṃ mā sṛjāmi*, *agne āyūṃṣi*, *adhvaryavo adribhiḥ*, *gomad ūrṣuṇā*, *sattyā tūtujānaḥ*, *sa havyavāṭ*, *sa na indrāya*, *madhvā yajñam accha*, *aya te asya*, *vāyo ye te*.

O Lord of the Forest, protect us; who shall deliver you from us? To the Lord of the Truth, the cows have come; indeed, to us, O Indra’s companion; [to us], O Indrāṇī; the turban; the Aśvins drank the Gharma; the Aśvins [drank] thirty-nine; one hundred and three.

Now follow those [verses] beginning with three feet that have the first syllable unaccented (*ādyudātta*): *svayambhūrasi*, *agnaye kavyavāhanāya*, *samidhāgnim*, *triḥ śaddhāmāsya*, *pratnānna hi teṣām*, *yyukṣvā hi deva*, *kṣapo rājan*, *bhadrā' utaibhirnaḥ*, *vītarṭha0*, *havirubhābhyām*, *devāyāṃ*, *phenena*, *kṣatrasya yoniḥ*, *dhānāvantaṃ karambhiṇam*, *aśvinakṛtasya te*, *maho'arṇaḥ*, *imamme suṣṭutirṭha0*, *sumatīvṛdhaḥ*, *yuñjantyasya*, *enā viśvānyabhi yajñam*.

Making Agni his banner, the great one [overcomes] the Vṛtras; let him kindle the fuel and invoke Mitra. O powerful Savitṛ, you two who strike down [enemies], [place] them in his body. Vāyu [is there]; may the earth be pleasant for him. One hundred and three. 4.

Now follow the three-footed verses with the middle syllable accented: *agnirmūrdhā divaḥ*, *trīṇi padā vicakrame*, *viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi paśyata*, *mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ*, *vimuñcadhvam*, *aṣāḍhāsi*, *sa idhānaḥ*, *bhadro no agniḥ*, *punāti te*, *yatte pavitram*, *codayitrī sūnṛtānām*, *tanūnapāt*, *asuryaḥ*, *dvāro devīḥ*, *agne svāhā*, *vāyur agregāḥ*, *abhīṣu naḥ*, *yad adya sūra udite*, *viśvebhir agne*, *pūṣan tava*, *dhartā divaḥ*. [Twenty-four. 5.

Now, those [verses] consisting of three feet and having the final syllable accented: *vītihotraṃ tvopaprayanto 'dhvaram*, *somānaṃ svaraṇam*, *yo revān na etu*, *yuñjāthāṃ rāsabhaṃ tam u tvā*, *sīrā yuñjanti*, *āpyāyasva sametu te*, *madintamaṃ madhumat*, *ayam agniḥ sahasriṇaḥ*, *ṛtajic ca ṛtaś ca*, *svatavāṃś ca*, *divo mūrdhā*, *hiraṇyapāṇim ūtaye*, *agnim dūtam*, *yuñjanti bradhnam*, *kas tvā āgacchati*, *svādiṣṭhayā*, *tisro devīḥ*, *barhiḥ*, *dvayam*.

Having joined [the hymns]: *kayā naścitra ā bhuvat*, *taraṇirviśvadarśataḥ*, *indravāyū bṛhaspatim*, *ime sutāḥ*, *tadviprāsaḥ*, *prajāpatau tvam*, *ṛcaṃ vācam*—these thirty-one [verses] constitute the sixth [section]. Now, among those with three feet, the words that have the acute accent on the final syllable (*antodātta*) are: *bheṣajamasi*, *ūrdhvā asya*, *kāvyayoḥ*, *rājāneṣu*, *devī dyāvāpṛthivī*, *devyo vamryaḥ*, *iyatyagre*—these six constitute the seventh [section].

Now follows the section on the three-footed verses with the *kampita* (trembling) accent: *pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ* (two verses), *revatī ramadhvam*, *niṣasāda dhṛtavatī*, *agnistigmena*, *payaḥ pṛthivyāḥ*, *nārirasyādade*, *adityai rāsnāsi*. These eight constitute the eighth [section].

Now follow the three-footed *jāti*s: *kastvā vimuñcati*, *tad viṣṇoḥ*, *yuktena manasā*, *indrasya syūḥ*, *apsv agne*, *adhā hy agne*, *preddho agne*, *agne ko 'si*, *bāhū me*, *svayaṃvāj*, *daivyā hotārā*, *ūrdhvaṃ madhvaram*. There are eleven [verses] from this point. Now follow those with a final *takāra* among the three-footed [verses]:
*āpavasva*, *parivājapatiḥ*, *ā te vatsaḥ*, *mano devahūḥ*, *yajño madhyā*, *ante pavitreṇa*, *punīhi yajā naḥ*. There are six [verses].

Now, those ending in *t* at the end of a three-footed verse: *ādhatte*, *ehi*, *tat savituḥ*, *abhyāvartasva*, *agnim*, *stomena*, *rakṣohā*, *viśvacarṣaṇiḥ*; [there are] seven [such instances]. (11) Now, those ending in *n* in the middle of a three-footed verse: *agniḥ*, *jyotiṣā*, *ut sakthyā*, *ava*, *kayā*, *tvam*; [there are] three [such instances].
(12) Now, those ending in *n* at the end of a three-footed verse: *ūrjam*, *vahanti*; [there are] three feet and two [instances]. (13)
Now, those with three internal divisions have the acute accent on the first syllable; for they come to me when the five days have arrived. 14.

Now, those [verses] consisting of four feet with two pauses, which have an unaccented (anudātta) middle, otherwise have their first and middle syllables accented. They are: *sā viśvāyuḥ*, *śarmāsi*, *mano jūtiḥ*, *yaṃ paridhiṃ*, *saṃ barhir atra*, *pitara āganma*, *gṛhā māgne*, *tvaṃ hy agne*, *anu tvā mātā*, *vasvy asi*, *sam akhye*, *pari mā prati panthām*, *sūryasya cakṣur bhavatam*, *na āpataye tvā*, *sante kārṣir asi*, *yatte soma*, *tvam aṅga*, *āvayo manaḥ*, *na devāḥ*, *gātuvido*, *devīr āpaḥ*, *eṣa vo garbhaḥ*.

For whomsoever yours is the wind, O Bṛhaspati; now, O Agni, [bring] the prize of the prize. You stand toward those of sun-like skin; you are Indra’s thunderbolt. So much is his; you, O Agni, with the days; being peaceful, O Vāyu, when Agni eats; those among the people; he who for us, O Lord of Food; of food, all forms, O Agni Aṅgiras; up the highest; that which is yours today; you, O Agni, the sacrificers; up from you the embryo; having sat down again; you are the one to be gathered together; of this [cow], O giver of every desire; where the plants are vigorous.

Of those herbs which bear fruit, may the Gandharvas protect them for me; strength be mine! Homage be to the serpents! Those arrows which are yours, or those which are yours—[those that are] in the three oceans, the eternal moon, and the fire of fire—for you, O Agni, [the seers] the Aṅgirases, the friends... such is that Agni by whom the ṛṣis [attained their goals]. Homage be to the blue-necked one! That weapon of yours, may it not strike our offspring! Innumerable thousands of blue-necked, white-throated ones [dwell] in heaven; those who are in the trees, those of living beings, those of the paths, those who...

The sacred fords, strength from the stone; those which have been released, O Paro-dharṣayas, where the arrows [go] like our prize. May they shine upon us; so do I go to you. Thus far is the form; they are obtained through the *yajus* verses: "The two paths," "May Aṅgiras raise us up," "Those of ours who were before," "O Soma, with the knee," "Sarasvatī with the mind," "She has anointed my limbs," "My head, O Narāśaṃsa," "He has breathed toward us," "Indra with his bay horses," "Indra the good protector, the self-strong," "Of him we [speak]," "With joyful songs," "He who is Indra."

Not with falsehood; Tvaṣṭṛ, the impeller, [has approached] the Lord of the Forest, he who breathes for the bipeds. O divine Adhvaryus, what indeed is the *brahman* equal to the Sun? He has come forth with a bright garment, the well-pleasing [portion] of the horse which is yours from the entrails. O you who possess the prize, that which is most swift, O Vāyu, the pure Tanūnapāt with his aids, the two *barhis* grasses, Indra, Indra—*svāhā*! With the wise ones, the *svāhā*-utterance of the gods, Agni, Tvaṣṭṛ, you are the hero Yama; the kindled [fire], the fearless Tanūnapāt, the paths...

With the bow they seized the cattle; Indra’s thunderbolt, the desire of the Maruts, made it cry out from that sacrifice, from that [sacrifice] the horses. That indeed is our kinship for the gods, the two forms, the two Medhas, O Agni, the host. I invoke the great one, as those who look toward the sun. Those who have been born for you, the fierce one, with the unassailable ones, through heroic deeds. May my prayers be supreme; may they prosper thus, by which the three rites are performed. You, O Agni, are the first; for the *iḍā*, Savitṛ, golden-handed, [offers] to you—those which are yours.

O Bhaga, O Praṇetṛ, O Ānas, O Sattya, when they bind [the fetus], arise! O Pādharta, may the wind be auspicious for us, may the sky be peace; from whatever place the embryo comes, may Agni, the god, [be] with Agni. Come here with the banner of the day, Svāhā! To Pūṣan! The navel has four corners; to Tapas, Svāhā! One hundred and eighty-one, minus one: 15.

Now, the four-footed verses with two unaccented syllables: With the *gāyatra* [meter], you are kindled. Both worlds. The full ladle; give it to me. The milk of the great ones. The bright [seed] of you, Agni. The birthplace of Agni. Wide, O Viṣṇu. For the sake of the two-fold purpose. These [oblations] are possessed of oblation. For the heart, you. To Vācaspati. Possessing good heroes, [grant] heroes. With offspring, [grant] offspring. The Brahmin. Adorable, lovely. Today, the essence of the waters. This is yours. In this, O gods. Be gracious. You are pleasant. For the sake of the young one. The intoxicating [Soma] has come. The vigorous one has sat down. Together with the ashes. The year. Along with consumption (*yakṣma*).

The drop has fallen; fashion your strength for food and wealth. Breathe upon me! By these two, O most radiant ones, you are indeed the best waters. Having drawn back the bow, you stand as the guardians of Truth. This is the enclosure of the waters, this is the finder of cattle. May Indra be with us against those [enemies]. Of their thoughts—seven seas, waves, and seed flow together; they stream forth together with the rain-drops, O much-invoked one. Like a wild beast on its back, may we attain the celestial. O gods, that sacrifice is the form of consecration, the form of hospitality. With the *praiṣas* [the Adhvaryu] performs the *praiṣas*; with the half-verses, the *ukthas* of the Aśvins.

May the morning libation purify us; may the *parisrut* juices, seeing thee, cleanse my back-bones as one released from a wooden post. By thy breath for me—three times threefold, according to the seasons—Indra [purifies] the great earth; with good sacrificial grass, Agni [purifies] the two young dawns. The three *iḍā*s, the divine *śamitr*, the offerings of strength, the gods among gods, the sacrificial grass of the waters—may Vāyu [grant] thee life. O friend, are you well? You are the seasons; according to the seasons, I ask about the half-months and the joints. This is the supreme altar of the gods; may there be auspiciousness and welfare for us.

"O Agni, these hundred goats are for you; [recite] 'The gods have come here to this sacrifice,' 'O divine Dawn and Night,' and these four [verses beginning with] 'These [fathers] who dwell at the ends of the earth, the father of many,' 'The loud sounds from heaven and earth,' 'Having encompassed all beings, [the sacrifice] has entered the consciousness,' 'May they encompass me,' 'For you, a thousand [oblations],' 'Down upon the supine one,' 'In the morning, to Agni,' and 'Now, for exhaustion, Svāhā!'—this is one hundred and one. (16)

Now, in the midst of those words whose first syllable is udātta, there are anudātta syllables: *dhūr asi*, *dhṛṣṭir asi*, *mayīdam agne*, *gṛhapate 'kr̥ṇma karmā*, *ādityās tvā*, *namo mitrasya*, *agne vratapāḥ*, *pari tvā girvano giraḥ*, *revatīr amaddhvam*, *māhir bhūr māgnāi*, *paktnīr anyām āvaha*, *yajña-yajñaṃ deva savitar*, *vātar̥ṭhaṃ bhava*, *vāje-vāje 'vata*, *somar̥ṭhaṃ rājānam*, *agne sahasva*, *somasya tvā*, *ā tvā jigharmi*, *pari tvāgne*.

Sit down, O Hotṛ, well-born with inspired luster; day after day, unwearied, the banner of all, Agni has been kindled. He has pierced Indra, the one who presses the soma and does not sacrifice; he has consumed the plants. "The Dispeller" is thy name, O Agni; thou art the fame and the vigor of the sacrifice for the life of every being. From joint to joint they grow forth. May Aditi awaken thee; Agni is the guardian of the people. To thee, most wonderful in fame, let our words go forth. Awake! Homage to thy weapon, O most bountiful one, most auspicious! Homage to thy heat, thou who art the eye of the gods.

Father Bṛhaspati, O Indra, protect these; go forward to their vital organs for him, for the divine Sustainer. Step forth with Agni for strength, Svāhā! On the head of the universe, the Brahman and the Kṣatra; the tiger, the form of Soma. O Aśvins, that which is here—by you indeed, O Agniṣvātta fathers, sitting upon the ruddy ones, by means of the Veda, in the form of Sarasvatī, in the womb, the brilliance of cattle, the hairs, the offering, the goddess measuring it out, Varuṇa, the Kṣatra, in which the horses [are].

The kindled fire [reaches] the divine doors, when, O gods, you two golden ones come; what are those among which yours are? How many are your auspicious chariots? When you have risen up for us—may Agni [protect] you! What [is given] for the horse, what for your mounting—that we desire from you. With one [verse] and not with you [alone], I kindle Indra with the *iḍā*-offerings; Indra, the two divine Hotṛ-priests, Tvaṣṭṛ, and the kindling Indra. I praise the great protector of the body, the piercer, the praised one. Of the two wide-extending [worlds], there are three well-approachable, well-formed, well-fashioned, and beautiful ornaments.

Enkindled, anointing both [worlds], you have gone forth; the two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first, well-spoken, are among those who have awakened. O Brahmins, may Bhāratī and the Pitṛs come to our sacrifice like a serpent with its coils. O Agni, glory be to you! You are Aditi of all; that is the nature of Sūrya, that is the nature of Mitra. O great Agni, O Indra, come hither to him. O Indra, for the one who is awake, today let the offering be prepared for the one who is alert. O Sinīvālī of broad hips, may the night be favorable for the bridegroom. O long-lived Agni, protect us on all sides.
For Indra, you are the Law (Dharma) of this mind. [Total: one hundred and thirty.]

Now follow the four-footed verses, which have the acute accent on the first syllable and the grave accents on the middle syllables: *agneḥ tanūḥ*, *etát te*, *kadā caná ayam agníḥ*, *etát te śivó náma*, *cít-patiḥ*, *má ṛk-sāmayoḥ śilpé*, *śvātrāḥ pītāḥ*, *eṣā te*, *agnáu agníḥ*, *yuñjáte mánaḥ*, *agreṇír asi*, *ghṛtám ghṛtapāvānaḥ*, *śvātrā stha*, *rāyá vayám*, *yajñó devānām*, *suśarmási*, *harír asi purudásmo vísurūpaḥ*, *satrásya ṛddhiḥ*, *yajñásya dóhaḥ*, *davasyáham*, *eṣásya aryamáṇam bṛhaspátim sávitāram*.

Having wiped the back of the waters like parents [wipe] their son, O Rudras, may the god release you with clarified butter. May the furrows, rich in horses, rich in Soma, and flowing downward, speak for you—a hundredfold—driving away consumption. O Agni, rule over this firm foundation; I meditate upon that Agni who is the embryo of the Adityas, he who is copper-colored, who by the purifying word is the Lord of Speech, higher than heaven, the roaring bull, the ocean. We worship him with this oblation. This breast, four-horned, the upholder of Truth...

The Truth-abiding one, the six-fold sacrifice, this very oblation-chamber they weave; the parched grains, the groats—this is the form of the parched grains. By the vow, [I offer] the consecration to the Fathers who receive the *svadhā* offering, and to the Aśvins. My eye, my tongue, the waters today. For the great Indra, three goddesses. With the oblation, the Protector Indra; the two Aśvins from Namuci. The two Aśvins, drink the oblation! Sutrāman. The goddess Earth. Three goddesses with the gods. May she go to her own place. Whichever way, upward this one; upward this one, the Mahānāmnīs.

The red, the silver, and the tawny ones—I ask you about their felling, their departure, and their settling. May it be so for us here and in the world beyond. And at every sacrifice, O two who delight in strength, the first offerings of vigor are released for you by your own will. The chariot-bearer is the oblation; the moon is gathered from the waters of the mind. Prajāpati moves as the longing one; this is my great prayer to Agni. Vibhrāṭ, the great and downward-turning, the gods are indeed full of clarity and rich in ghee.
I am the bull of the worlds; you are our father. O two-fold one, swell us with nourishment from the quarters! Svāhā to Speech, to Yama! One hundred and thirteen. 18.

Now follow the four-footed verses with the accent on the middle syllable: *yad grāme 'vabhṛtha nicumpuṇa*, *viśvo devasya*, *iyantaścid asi mitraḥ*, *na irāvati apām peruḥ*, *ye devāsaḥ*, *citram devānām*, *sam id raṇo dhātā rātiḥ*, *sugā vo vyathir hi indraś ca*, *kakubham rūpam*, *śanno bhavantu vācas te*, *imām ud uttiṣṭha ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇaḥ*, *oṣadhayaḥ prati*, *mitraḥ sṛjya sinīvālī sukāparde*, *utthāya bṛhatī*, *dṛśāno rukmo antaḥ*, *agne śivaḥ*.

Having become [this], we know your purpose; O Agni, that [is] from heaven, homage, well-sacrificed, to the plants. In the *aśvattha* tree is your [abode]; since these [plants] are yours, grant me long life, O Son of Strength (*ūrj*). You are the Earth, the germ, the firm dwelling, the firm womb, the nest-maker, the butter-rich, the soil of the earth. O Indra and Agni, [protect] the unshaking [earth]. Having released the fuel-stick, that which is yours, O Rudra, the auspicious one—may the blue-throated one go around us. Those gods who are so many, who approach, who among the gods are the givers of out-breath and in-breath, [they are to be honored] with oblations.

Growing strong, they have sacrificed for you, sharpening [the flame]—you whose work we follow, O Agni, with a thousand eyes, offering oblations, fair of countenance, like the current of a river in its forward rush. May he be ours, the Lord of the world; Indu is skill, Indra is the knower, the altar is the one who makes known. He whom you, O Agni, carry as a carrier of offerings, and those others—just as King Soma is to us, so are the limbs, the milk, the jar, the entrails, the waters in the place of the womb. Where the gods are, where the three [sacrificial fires] are, where the sacred word (*brahman*) is, where Indra is kindled—there is Indra.

May the Lord of the Forest, rejoicing in the sacrificial grass, release the drops of ghee for Dawn and Night; may the two divine Hotṛ-priests, the physicians, with the spring season as the fifth, seize this [oblation]. You are the tethering-rope for Prajāpati; the sun is yours, the moon is yours. Who has milked this? Sixfold is his Hotṛ-priest; let him worship Prajāpati, whose these are, who is the self-giver. Let him worship that Lord. Aditi is the sky; may we have good cattle and good heroes. May the years be favorable to you, O increaser of food and wealth. The waters indeed, with their forward-moving teams and their yoked horses, have come to us at dawn, like the Hotṛ of Indra.

The Yakṣas, the three goddesses, the two who delight in the prayer, the one for whom the sacrificial grass is strewn, between Mitra and Varuṇa, those three, they shall speak here of you, standing on the chariot, O Ṛjīti, the protector, indeed the god of this [prayer], at the end of old age, all the gods, toward Vāyu, in whom [is] the invincible, the sleepless, O Aśvins, Bhaga who conquers at dawn, [the cows] rich in horses and rich in cattle, bring these to the living, all the quarters, Heaven and Earth, Agni with the heart, in whom [are] all, both prosperity and knowledge;
forty-one hundred and one. 19.

Now follow the four-footed verses with the final syllable accented: *avante devaśrutau*, *deveṣvacchinnasya te*, *sa prathamas te naḥ*, *arvanto 'gneya gṛhapataye*, *yasya prayāṇam*, *dyus te pṛṣṭham*, *nihotā sarṭhaṃ sīdasva*, *āpo devīr nābhā pṛthivyāḥ*, *udeṣām bāhū divas pari*, *śrīṇām udāraḥ*, *iḍām agne tā asya*, *nirveśanaḥ saṅgamanaḥ*, *sagarajñīr bahvīm*, *mā va riṣat*, *pāvakavarcāḥ śukravarcāḥ*, *ṛtāvānam mahiṣam*, *ayā śatena samyak*.

Flow forth, O Agni, against those who are born; drive them away with your cooking-female flames. Scatter them about from your bow, O Red One! He who is our father, sun-rayed, golden-haired, this measurer of the earth, ascending to heaven—I offer that thought of Savitṛ. Ghee has been sprinkled; may all [the gods] eat today. These two of yours, when from your intention they reached the abode—Agni, the seat, the form; may he cause them to hear with the *iḍā*-invocations. The portions for consumption, rich in spirituous liquor, seated upon the sacrificial grass—whatever is your essence, you, O Soma, together with the fathers; you, O Agni, [together with] the Aśvins.

Into the mouth of the true sovereign I place [thee]; they sprinkle [thee] around, O praised one. By the gods, by Dawn and Night, for Indra, let the Soma be drunk. May the Aśvins grant us medicine; Savitṛ and Varuṇa are the two physicians who bring forth [remedies]. What was the sky? Among the hosts, thou art the mother; and who among them knows this? I know it, O Prajāpati. The Maruts with spotted horses [are here], and together with Prajāpati’s fervor these [beings] have come toward thee. The eastern seat, the wide-spreading sacrificial grass—so great is he, from that [comes] the Virāj; not of him... [is there end].

Hear from me that which was born, O you of listening ears! Today all the Rudras and the Viśvedevas have come to me with offerings. O Indra, the gods desire you as a god; they seek you. Not by days nor by nights—like Bhaga—did the seven seers behold you, the protector of the cow-pen. "That darkness is in me," [he said]; "we two are indeed different; there is one hundred minus one. 20.

Now, among those consisting of four feet, those which have the udātta accent on the final syllable are: *saṃsravabhāgā asya*, *yeṣām adhvaryo*, *mā ṣū ṇaḥ*, *tryāyuṣaṃ jamadagneḥ*, *vasumato rudra*, *te mūrdhānam diva ākramya*, *vājinn udakramoḥ*, *naktoṣāsā*, *samanasā yāsu*, *iṣkartāram adhvarasya*, *vijyā dhanuḥ*, *imā rudrāya*, *viśvakarmā vimanāḥ*, *samiddhe agnau*, *etāvad rūpam*, *agniṣvāttān ṛtumataḥ*, *idaṃ pitṛbhyaḥ*, *tad asya rūpam*, *āntrāṇi sthālīḥ*, *yo bhūtānām*.

The kindled fire, O Aśvins; may Vāta [protect] us; Tvaṣṭṛ alone; the invincible Jātavedas; the greatness of Narāśaṃsa; he who was born at once; the sweet seat; the fathers; that sacrifice; do not [neglect] the spy; the golden-handed Asura; may Mitra be gracious; the bull Savitṛ has bellowed; this first thing moves—forty-nine. 21.

Now, the four-footed [verses]: "O you who are born first, who stand in the purifier, whose essence is grain; with the Ādityas you have eaten. Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Agni, you are the filler of the soil. O gods, you are our protectors. Of that [god] of true impetus, of Viṣṇu—[the verse] *nukaṃ* (RV 1.22.20). That [verse] *pratad viṣṇuḥ* (RV 1.154.2). You are the portion of the Rākṣasas. O divine waters, [you are] the protector of water. You belong to Savitṛ. From the sin committed against the gods—[the verse] *sa imā naḥ* (RV 10.128.9). O gods, you are the fillers of the soil. O Agni, you are the filler of the soil. Like a mother to her son, [you are] the ruler, the well-winged one. Flow toward us, O god, you who are the filler of the soil. O Agni..."

Thine is the Ashvin splendor from the flowing food; like a ram, like a sheep, thou art vast in measure. That which is there, that which is yonder, that which is the oblation—thy body, O Lord of the Forest, with strong limbs, wherewith the sky [is reached], Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuna, may it go forth to Brahmaṇaspati on a chariot easy to drive, like a horse. We magnify thee, O Mighty One, for thou art the lord of this; a hundred and thirty more. 22.

Now, the four-footed verses in the middle: *jātyāgne*, *tvaṃ viṣṇorarāṭam*, *indrasyasyūḥ*, *parivīrasya*, *agneranīkam*, *abhibhūrasi*, *yuje vā*, *sujāto jyotiṣā*, *mūrddharvā'si*, *rāḍayampuro harikeśaḥ*, *pañcā juhvānā*, *sarasvatyaśvinā tejasā*, *sa tvanno*, *yadvāto devī',* *uṣāsā naktendrasya rūpam*, *paridyāvāpṛthivī*, *vidadyayadī tvanno',* *agne pathaspathaḥ*, *paripātamimā giraḥ*, *pranūnaṅkṣatrasya tvā*.
Twenty-three [verses]. 23.

Now, the last [verse] among the four-footed [verses] in the middle: "O Ghṛtācī, you are Ghṛtācī; you stand here. They have eaten, they have rejoiced. You who are fair to behold, O God Savitṛ, this is yours. Never do you fail us. We have become the offspring of Prajāpati, golden-hued. And the protection of the highest dawns from the furthest distance. Those divine armies, the waters—be mindful of me! Again, [I take] that splendor of yours which is in heaven. Yoke the ploughs; the furrow is rich in heroes. The plants are established upon the earth. And that Brahman which was born... [your].

Bhramāsaḥ! Prajāpati has spoken to you, the seer, the messenger of all. Those who have not spoken to us, do not [speak] to the great one. O Viśvakarman, those which are your supreme abodes, go forth, O Agni, with the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), and the animals. May our ancestors, those who are consumed by the fire (*agniṣvātta*), come to the animals for us. To that god Indra, to Sarasvatī, and to the *barhis*—[may they come]. Three times has the sun been sharpened by the rein. With auspicious ears, may Mitra not look upon us with [hostile] intent. With sovereign power, O Agni, drive away [the enemies].

With Indra as your own seat, may the chariot follow you; it becomes like that of a thundercloud. With three feet it stands above; therefore, from the sacrifice, that which was in the Puruṣa—three hundred and sixty [verses]. When Indra struck Vṛtra, [he took] six [of them] for the Sūrya among the gods. For by means of the deity, this praise belongs to the gods. Homage be to you! Prajāpati, while being gathered together, performing his work, encompassed sixty-four [verses]. 24.

Now follows the four-footed *kāmya* [offering]: "By form, by power, O companion in joy, thou who art resplendent, I take up the waters; advancing with the *gāyatra* [meter], come hither! May they release me from this great [evil] with the healing medicine of the Aśvins; well-being, self-existent—[this is] the twenty-fifth [verse] regarding the ten [parts] of the steed."

Now, while the four-footed [earth] is trembling, Antaka [says]: "I take the second purifier of Vasu, acceptable to Agni, for the sake of truth, for the performer of the sacrifice. You are firm with splendor; may this man be firm. O Agni, lead him within. Within the ocean, within the waters, for Sarasvatī, for Speech. O gods, enter from all sides! Let the released ones flow forth with the Vasus. Sharpen me. In the ocean you [are]; he shall fight. All things—you are the highest. O Agni, yours is the fame. Rise up, O Agni, with your own powers. That which is auspicious to you, O Rudra..."

His body is non-terrible; he who glides forth with arrow-handed [attendants] rushes against the cattle-pens. I yoke Agni for you; sprinkle him all around, O fathers seated upon the sacrificial grass, with bright milk. Indra is the good protector; may the two physicians, Tanūpā and Indradu, [protect us]. Like the Kavaṣyas, [may] the Aśvins [come] with cows. You are brilliance; let the Vasus anoint you. The Gāyatrī and Triṣṭubh meters are your heaven. May it not burn you from above. Protect us; do not abandon our strength nor the one for whom the sacrificial grass is well-prepared. Even the waters have extended toward our sacrifice.
The moon [is] in the waters; these five rivers, you [are they], together with the hymns, the Asuryas by name, in a golden vessel—fifty-five.
26. Now follows the four-footed, two-kampa [verse]: "The heaven, as it were, has been enclosed by abundance in the forests; you are the second in the ocean"—these are four. 27.

Now follow the four-footed verses with two *jīti*s: 1. *vasoḥ pavitram asi tanūpā agne* (The purifier of wealth art thou, O Agni, protector of the body). 2. *sanno sindhuḥ* (May the river be favorable to us). 3. *pavitre sthaḥ* (Ye two are the purifiers). 4. *sthiro bhava* (Be firm). 5. *apeta vīta* (Depart, go away). 6. *sa dudravat* (Let it flow swiftly). 7. *kanyā iva vahatum* (Like a maiden to the wedding procession). 8. *vāyo agne trijātyo hotādhvaryur brāhmaṇo 'sya somaḥ* (O Vāyu, O Agni, the three-born Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu, the Brāhmaṇa—his Soma). 9. *dhenum trir āyuṣyaṃ varcasyam* (The cow, thrice-life-giving, bestowing luster). (There are sixteen [syllables]). 28.

Now, among the four-footed [verses], those ending in *t*: *ahṛtam asi*, *divo vā jyotir asi*, *yas te drapsaḥ skandati*, *ko adāt*, *somasya tviṣir asi*, *agne bṛhan*, *hṛtsat*, *śuciṣat*, *saṃjñānam asi*, *hiraṇyagarbhaḥ*, *saṃ varcasā*, *tvaṣṭuḥ prajāta-aśvaḥ*, *kṛdhi svid āsīt*, *viśvataścakṣuḥ*, *uta vājasya mā*, *somaṃ adbhyaḥ svāhā*, *yajñaṃ varuṇaḥ*, *yad asyāḥ*, *deva barhiḥ*, *indra deva-indraḥ*, *catasro deva barhiḥ*, *vayodhasaṃ devaḥ*.

Narāśaṃsa with the four Ādityas; Bhāratī for us; that which Akraṇda; what was given by Yama; he who has golden horns; he who makes [the world] resound; the thousand-headed one; "I know this today"; O gods; the transverse one; stretched out; he blew away; we meditate upon; by power; beyond death; that eye; the unmoving; the one; another indeed; three; forty-one more—twenty-nine.

Now, the four-footed verses ending in *n* at the end are as follows: *ye rūpāṇi*, *tantvā*, *śociṣṭha*, *ava rudram*, *sa prathamaḥ*, *iḍe rante*, *yuñjānaḥ prathamam*, *hasta ādhāya*, *pratūrtam*, *vājin*, *saṃ vasothāmā*, *tvāhārṣam*, *prati spaśaḥ*, *yāmiṣum*, *śivena vacasā*, *drāpe*, *andhasaḥ*, *viśvakarman*, *haviṣā*, *balavijñāya*, *sthaviraḥ*, *indrasya vṛṣṇaḥ*, *indre mām*, *pañca diśaḥ*, *vayan nāma*, *vājasya nu*, *yad dattam*, *yatra dhārāḥ*, *indrasya*.

Indra is the illusion of form; he who knows this belongs to Varuṇa. Who indeed is the Sun alone? First, I have performed the praise of Dadhikrāvan. Among the five, him with the ancient [praise]. The horse [is] with clarified butter. All moments [are] the sacrifice of the gods. Indra and Vāyu, O fair to behold! Indra and Agni. From the father, you swell for the Aśvins. Fierce with blood. Forty. 30.

Now follow four-footed verses ending in *nakāra* (the letter *n*). Again: *mano 'yan no agnir upāvīr asy utkrāmākkrandad agniḥ sīdattvam ayam agnir vīratamo ye 'nneṣv indraṃ daivīstridhā hitam agnir asmi janmanā nānā hi yamaśvinā devīrdvāra indraṃ devīs tisro dvāro vayodhasaṃ devīs tisro ghṛtenāñjanyat puruṣaṃ yajñena yajñaṃ rucam̐ brāhmam ārodasī divi pṛṣṭo 'ṣṭau vyakkhyadye naḥ sapatknāḥ*.
Twenty-six [verses]. 31.

Now, the four-footed verses ending in *nakāra*: "mitro no" (*mitro naḥ*), "yā ta ādityebhyas tvā" (*yā ta ādityebhyaḥ tvā*), "catustrirṛśat tantavaḥ" (*catustriṃśat tantavaḥ*), "mā na indra" (*mā na indra*), "te yutkāya" (*te yutkāya*), "savitā śivo bhava" (*savitā śivaḥ bhava*), "dṛḍhā hrasva devi" (*dṛḍhā hrasva devi*), "daṃṣṭrābhyām mṛḍayā juṣak" (*daṃṣṭrābhyām mṛḍaya juṣak*), "pāvako dharuṇa ito jajñe" (*pāvakaḥ dharuṇaḥ itaḥ jajñe*), "vātasya jūtim sahasā jātām" (*vātasya jūtim sahasā jātām*), "lokampṛṇa kṛṇu" (*lokampṛṇa kṛṇu*), "svit vanam ka u so" (*svit vanam kaḥ u saḥ*), "yā senā" (*yā senā*), "īdṛkṣāsa etādṛkṣāsa etarṭhaḥ" (*īdṛkṣāsaḥ etādṛkṣāsaḥ etarṭhaḥ*), "sadhasttham sīsena tantram manasā" (*sadhasttham sīsena tantram manasā*).

*Tvaṣṭā dadhad āt it*, *indraḥ*, *dūrāt tvām agne vṛṇate*, *ājuhvāna īḍyaḥ*, *ya ime te ācaranti*, *suparṇaṃ vaste*, *nābhyā āsīt*, *akṛṣṇe pravāvṛje*, *śammanvatīr iyate*, *śaṃ vātaḥ*, *kravyādam agnim*—these are thirty-one (31). Now follow the four-footed verses with acute accent on the first syllable: *santvam pratad ātatam*, *it tam in naḥ*, *māha tvan naḥ*, *na vai tvām it*, *satvan naś citram*, *māṃ pratad vocet*, *dan tvā hi mandra*—these are eighteen (18). 33.

Now, those [verses] which have three pauses and are accented on the first syllable: *agne brahma*, *vasubhyaḥ*, *tavorugāya*, *uddivam aty anyān*, *mano yāhi*, *tantum pra*, *viśve devāsaḥ*, *ātiṣṭha*, *idam id u tyat*, *prajāpate*, *nādityai rāsnā*, *ṛco nāma*, *aśvinā chāgasya*, *yaṅkrandasi*, *daivyāv adhvaryū*, *brahmaṇas pate*, *dṛte dṛṃha*, *ha mā*, *anādhṛṣṭā purastāt*, *viśvāsāṃ bhuvāṃ svāhā prāṇebhyo lomabhyaḥ*. There are twenty-four [syllables]. 34.

Now follow those with three pauses and an initial low-pitched accent (*anudātta*): *yuṣmā indraḥ*, *savitustveṣā te*, *agnirjyotirvrataṃ kṛṇuta*, *indraprāṇo'yam*, *venomarttvān*, *indramahām*. 2 || *indramahām*. 2 ||

"Indra, who by his might; the Lord of Speech, seated firmly within thee; cook for the Aśvins! Truly, O friend, Viśvakarman [cooks] thee; two [verses] for Parameṣṭhin; two [verses] for thee, the sweet one; behold this oblation, the form of Truth; in the favor of Vaiśvānara; may Vaiśvānara Agni come for our protection; the Rishi [sings] for Yama; for thee, for the ocean; for thee, for the ocean—twenty-six [verses]. 35.

Now, at the third pause, there is a tremor (*kampa*). "I pour out; heaven has invited me; the tremor is born of the lineage, established for the sake of the goal. For my intention, for the impulse, thou art the path to heat. Thou art great; thou art barley. Guard me from the two waters. From the mountain, do not strike this one. Two [verses] in the intermediate space has the Great One sat down. (1) "Indra, thunderbolt in hand; that breast of thine which is terrible"—seventeen [syllables]. (2) Now, at the third pause, the first halves have the acute accent (*udātta*). "O Vāyu, come hither; those vessels of the wise, the offerings of strength, proceed. O divine Agni, thou art the head; the seed, the urine. And Agni Vaiśvānara’s favor"—nine [syllables]. (3)

Now follow those [verses] which have three pauses and are accented on the final syllable: *gandharvastvopahūtā*, *ihaivāgne*, *vivasvannādityai jatu*, *daśamāsyo agniḥ paśuḥ*, *athaitānaṣṭau*, *āsute dasrā yuvākavaḥ*, *syonā pṛthivi*, and *ahāni śam ekādaśa*. (38)

Now, at the end of the three-verse sections, there are single *jāti* verses: "Before the cruel one, [is] thy seat; may the waters not abandon us. Anointed with ghee, thou art taken with a support; thou art firm (*dhruva*). May he be dear to us, the filler of the soil. Truth and sweetness, and the bright and the pure. O Agni, do thou [grant] us the nearest life through sacrifice. Truly indeed! To Prajāpati thee! These [verses], as they are, over us—depart! Twenty-one. (39) Now, at the end of the three-verse sections, there are double *jāti* verses: "Who art thou? Great art thou! Indra, manly, filling the people. Might and splendor, heat—five. (40)

Now, at the end of the third [section], those with the second half-verse accented are: *ādityāstvak*, *soma rājan*, *indravāyū ime*, *indrāgnī āgatam*, *omāsaścarṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ*, *indra marutvataḥ*, *javo yaḥ ṣoḍaśī*, *stomo'gniṛtuthā*, *hotāram*, *namo'stu rudrebhyaḥ*, *dvistrayā devāḥ*, *yadāpaḥ*, *prāṇāya svāhā*, *bṛhaspate'ti*, *indra gomantam*, *indrāyāhi*, *agniṛṣiḥ*, *gāyatram chandaḥ*, *payaso retaḥ*. Twenty. 41.

Now, those ending in *t* at the third pause: *tvam agne vratapāḥ*, *idam āpaḥ*, *bṛhaspatisutasya*, *viśvakarman haviḥ*, *indrasya vajro 'si*, *āmā kṣatrasya ulbam*, *nābhiḥ meṣṭau*. (42) Now, those ending in *n* at the third pause: *bhadro me sajoṣāḥ*, *indre haratiḥ*, *ūrdhvo bhava*, *yadā pipeṣa*, *pañca*. (43) Now, those with the second vowel as the acute (*udātta*) at the first [pause] among those ending in *t* at the third pause: *ukhāṃ kṛṇotu*, *kutas tvam*, *dviḥ*. (44)
Now, at the pause after three syllables, the first syllable is acute (*udātta*): *edandyāmmā dviḥ*.

(45) Now, at the pause after the final syllable, the first syllable is acute: *mā bheragne dabdhāyo'ndhastthasvāhā*, *yajñam̐ varuṇasyottambhanaṃ*, *devīrāpaḥ śuddhā voḍḍhvaṃvvācante*, *dvitīyaṃ svāṅkṛto'si*, *somaḥ pavate*, *yaste'aśvasanivrēśīnāntvā vasavastrayodaśākṣareṇa*, *ye devā'gninetrā vasavastvā dhūpayantu*, *ākūtimagniṃ*, *viṣṇoḥ kkramo'si*, *cidasi*, *tayā''yurme*, *navavirṭha0śattyā stuvata*, *tantunā rāyaspoṣeṇa*.

You are the mistress of the heap; for the guileless, for the bold, for the auspicious one, for the leafy one—vigor and preeminence, welfare and splendor, the stone and wealth, one and four, and the three-year-old [victim]—the praised one, the sacrificial grass soft as wool, well-fashioned, the two divine dawn-dames, the three goddesses, the four, the two Aśvins, Sarasvatī, the four, Agni Sviṣṭakṛt—you today [are invoked] for the eastern wind, for the stars—those two, the three-year-old [victim], for the Gāyatrī, for the earth—the moles, the wind with the breath, with the support—fuel for you, sixty-one. 46.

Now, at the end of the *atyāvasāna* sections, the first syllables are unaccented (*anudātta*). "Oṣe tvā," "Agnestanūḥ," "Indraghoṣas tvā rakṣohaṇam valagahanam," "Rakṣohaṇo vaḥ," "Mitrasya mā," "Ākūtaye me," "Uśik tvam āpaye svāhā," "Eṣa te nirṛte," "Āvir maryāḥ," "Ūrdhvām āroha," "Agniḥ pṛthuḥ," "Savitā prasavitā," "Apāntvā," "Ayam puraḥ," "Iyam upari," "Sajūr ṛtubhiḥ," "Anaḍvān vayaḥ," "Pṛthivī chandaḥ," "Agnir devatā," "Āchando virāḍ asi," "Trayaḥ prāṇaś ca satyañ ca," "Tisro rayiś ca."

Rice grains and fire; two for Mitra; four for Agni; two for the six-year-old ox; three for the Aśvins; "I choose thee first for Agni, Svāhā! For the Hiṅkāra, for Prāṇa, for the waters, for the earth!"—smoke-colored ones for Spring; six-year-old oxen for Virāj; men for Prajāpati; the mayu-beast for Prajāpati; the human wild beast for the Moon; gnats for the hair; the shoulders of the Maruts for dancing; the bard for the Ṛta; the heart of a thief for Death. (Fifty-five. 47.

Now, at the end [of the section], there are those with the acute accent on the final syllable: "This is your portion, O Rudra; you are self-ruling, the slayer of rivals. "For Agni, you who have the *gāyatrī* metre. "May the Vasus fashion you. "You are sovereign. "For the one dwelling among men, *veṭ*! First, the black-necked ones belong to Agni. The humpbacked bull and the black ones belong to the Earth; these are mentioned first and second as the common animals (*sañcara*). The smoke-colored ones, appearing tawny, belong to Prajāpati. The crane belongs to Sūrya. The male and female porcupine belong to the Days and Nights. The hedgehog belongs to the Seasons. The white-spotted one belongs to the Ādityas. Pūṣan is associated with the *vaniṣṭhu*.

From the rivers, a fisherman; for Sandhi, a paramour; from the depressions, one who seizes with the mouth; for Kubjamā, a wood-gatherer; for Manyu, an iron-worker; for Yama, a driver of horses; from the lakes, a gambler; for Akṣarāja, a gamester; for Pratiśrutkā, a howler; for Agni, a fat man—twenty-eight [in total]. 48.

Now, at the very end, there is one born of the same species: "Thou art a cock; I generate thee for procreation. "O Agni, Lord of Vows, this is thy Gāyatrī. "Thou art firm; [I offer] to the Earth, to the Gods, to Heaven, to the Vasus; may Aditi support thee. "This is the measure of a thousand; homage to the Swift One. "These are mine: strength and gain, and the ladles. "The divine Agni, to whom [belongs]... *Svāhā!* To Kāya, to the second Agni, *svāhā!* To Āyu with the sacrifice. "Two ruddy ones, smoke-colored and ruddy, pure-haired"—these three are declared as the wandering [animals]. The fair-winged one belongs to Parjanya.

The rhinoceros belongs to the Viśvedevas; the wing of the fire-altar to Brahmā; the Brāhmaṇa to austerity; the potter to the vital joints; the elephant-driver to loathsomeness; and the scavenger to the Ekatriṃśa—forty-nine.

Now, at the end, there is a shaking. "O Earth, place for the sacrifice to the gods! O Aditi, the womb! O Agni, go to the ocean! You are the first, self-made; you are the light-maker. Four shakings: at the station of Iḍā, Tanūnapāt, Sarasvatī, Narāśaṃsa—these are two shakings. "The doors, the quarters, for strength, Svāhā! For Soma, the Kuluṅga bird; for Indra and Agni, the wing; for Agni Anīkavant; for Agni Gāyatra, the Narma bird; for Pūṃścalū. "May there be good friends for us"—this is the eighteenth [section]. 50.

Now, at the end of the last section, there is a single *jātya* chant: "For the being thee! Viṣṇu in heaven; thou art a lioness, thou art brilliance, bestow brilliance upon me! From Brahman, the horse, the hornless goat, the *śilpā*s, the *vaiśvadevī*s—these [are for Indra and Agni]; the second [set] has black-necked [goats]; the third [set] has black-necked [goats] for Agni; ten [in total]. Now, at the end of the last section, there is a double *jātya* chant: "Unspilled today art thou, O Āgrayaṇa! This is from the north; the swift, the threefold, the ocean, the windy, the speckled, the cross-speckled—the third [set] has black-necked [goats] for Agni; the fire-drills for Agni; the half-months; the breast of Indra—nine."

Then, at the end, there are three *jātya* [verses]. "Thou art a lioness; for Mitra and Varuṇa, thee!"—six *jātyas*. "For Madhava, thee! For Agni, thee! For me, thee!"—four *jātyas*. "From the abode of the earth, thou art spread out; from the first, with the second, four *jātyas*. To Madhava, svāhā! With teeth gnashing, nine. (53)

Now, at the end, those ending in *n*: "May my mind [be offered] to Agni Anīkavat, to the spring, the *kapiñjala* birds; to the ocean, the *śiśumāra* crocodiles; to Soma, the *ṛkṣa* bears; to Agni, the *kuṭaru* wildcats; to Soma, the *lava* partridges; to Indra, the *pārāvata* doves; to the Vasus, the *ṛśya* antelopes; to Īśāna, the *parasvata* wild asses—ten. (54)

Now, those that have no pause (*niravasāna*) are indeed accented on the first syllable. "Homage to you, O Indra, and the Maruts, and all the gods (*viśvedevāḥ*) in the cup! "The biting serpents have been driven away. "Ascend toward the north. "The *chandas* (meter) with one [verse]. "They praise with the *vaśa-chandas*. "To Babhluśa, to Rohita, to Kṛtsna, to Uṣṇīṣin. "To the releasing ones, to the assemblies (*sabhābhyaḥ*), to the hosts (*gaṇebhyaḥ*), to the carpenters (*takṣebhyaḥ*), to the horses (*aśvebhyaḥ*). "To the short one, to the wild one. Twenty-five. 55.

Now, in the case of those without a pause (*niravasāna*), they are unaccented (*anudātta*). "For my breath, Soma being carried forward... (Pūṣan with five syllables); "He has stood for the sake of the goal"; "I have mounted the western direction"; "The birds praised with nine [verses] upwards"; "With the ray for truth"; "The opening verse is Agni today"; "A good standing today"—these are twelve. (56) Now, in the case of those without a pause, there is a shake (*kampa*): "Thou art black; may [the waters] be sweet for us"; "Parameṣṭhin has addressed [thee]"—this is three times.
(57) Now, in the case of those without a pause, there is a shake of the *jātya* type: "Thou art the ocean"; "Agni with one syllable"; "The portion of barley"—this is three times. (58)

Now, at the conclusion, one of noble birth praised with nine [verses]: "Homage to the golden-armed one; homage to the one with matted hair, to the one who moves along the path, to the wind-like one, to the one who reaches the further shore"—seven (59).
Now, at the conclusion, two of noble birth [praised]: "You are the eager one, the bull-wave; for the eldest, for the one who wears a turban, for the one who moves in a herd"—five (60).

Now, at the conclusion, three of noble birth [praised]: "For the one of the well, for the one of the spring; you are the portion of Agni, you are the portion of the Vasus; for the sandy one, for the dry one"—six (61).

Now, [the mantras] with no pause (niravasāna) or a pause in the middle (madhyāvasāna): "dvitīyaśarmā," "asyagne," "vvājajit," "bhūḥ," "asi," "ādade," "rāvā," "asi," "dvirjātyam," "indrāya tvā," "bṛhadvate"—these are five.

(62) Now, those with four pauses (caturavasāna), which have the acute accent on the first syllable (hyādyudātta): "pratyuṣṭṛṃ," "rakṣaḥ," "indhānāstvā," "tryambakaṃ," "dhāmāni," "uśmāsi," "mahirbbhūḥ," "mā," "pṛdākuḥ," "agne pavasva," "adṛśramasya," "vvājī," "kanikkradat," "edho'si," "indrasyaujaḥ," "stha," "svāhā rudrāya"—these are eleven. (63)

Now, at the end of the fourth [section], those beginning with an *anudātta* accent are as follows: *agnīṣomayorujjitim*, *dvikampāḥ*, *sajūrdevena*, *aṃśuraṃśuṣṭe*, *agnīṣomābhyām*, *marutvantaṃ vṛṣabham*, *uttiṣṭhannojasā*, *yuvaṃ tam*, *devasyāham*, *prathamo devasya*, *tvā pṛthivyāḥ*, *suparṇo'si*, *virāḍ jyotiḥ*, *imaṃ stomam*, *sāhasram*, *tisro vāyoḥ*, *pūtaḥ punantu mā pitaraḥ*, *saṃvatsaro'si*, *agnimadya*, *ubhayoḥ*, *ṛjave tvā*, and *hiraṇmayena pātreṇa*. Thus there are twenty-two [verses].
Thus ends the *Manaḥsvāra-śikṣā* composed by the great seer Yogiyājñavalkya.
